newsitem.title: USA: Clinton approval rating hits record 64 percent.
newsitem.headline: Clinton approval rating hits record 64 percent.

text.p: The economy's strong performance has lifted President Clinton's job approval rating to a record 64 percent, according to a new ABC News/Washington Post poll released Wednesday.

The rise in Clinton's approval rating -- up from 56 percent last month -- coincides with new record highs this week in consumer confidence and the stock market, as measured by an 11-year-old ABC News/Money magazine poll.

It was only the second time since taking over the presidency in 1993 that Clinton's approval rating exceeded 60 percent in the poll, and the first time -- when it reached 63 percent -- was during his second month in office.

Seventy-nine percent of Americans think the balanced budget deal reached between the White House and Congress in May will ultimately fail to produce a balanced budget, and two-thirds think Congress is unlikely to enact campaign finance reform.

Fifty-one percent of Americans see just as much "partisan bickering as ever" in Washington, while 43 percent think Clinton and the Republican leaders of Congress were working together better than ever.

More good news for Clinton: Seventy-four percent of Americans say they're not interested in a sexual harassment lawsuit by Paula Jones, a former Arkansas state employee who says Clinton asked her to perform a sex act in a Little Rock hotel room in 1991.
Seventy-eight percent of the people surveyed said the case has not affected their opinion of Clinton.
Fifty-nine percent say they're also not interested in the investigation into the failed Whitewater land deal that has dogged the Clinton administration for years.
Forty-six percent of Americans believe the president did some illegal in the Whitewater scandal, but 65 percent said the case has not affected their opinion of Clinton.
Forty percent of Americans approve of the way Congress is doing its job and 53 percent disapprove.
The ABC/Washington Post poll was conducted July 6-8 among 1,017 randomly selected adults. It has a margin of error of three percentage points.

In the separate ABC/Money poll, the "Consumer Comfort Index" rose to a record plus 10 on the scale of plus 100 to minus 100. Fifty-seven percent of the respondents said the economy was in good shape, 62 percent said their finances were okay, while 46 percent said this was a good time to buy things.
At various points in the early 1990s, as many as 93 percent rated the economy negatively, compared to 43 percent today.

The index represents a rolling average based on telephone interviews with about 1,000 adults nationwide each month. This week's results were based on 1,017 interviews in the month ending July 6 and has an error margin of three percentage points.
